creator: Claude
name: Worn Workbench
source_format: MagicaVoxel VOX v150 (SIZE, XYZI, RGBA), single model

derived.glb_note: Derived from the .vox by tools/claude/export_glb.py; do not edit by hand. Linear COLOR_0 vertex colours, one material.

resolution_rationale: 0.05 m chosen deliberately over the suggested 0.10 m. A 0.10 m block-out read as a toy: top, shelf, apron and drawer all became 10 cm slabs (2-4x real timber) and the vise and the brief's tools collapsed into single cubes. At 0.05 m the 10 cm laminated top, 10x10 cm legs and 5 cm shelf boards match real construction timber and the vise jaws, T-handle, saw, hammer and drawer read at the three-quarter camera, while the occupied count stays far below the 10k furniture budget.
godot_mapping: godot = ((vx - px) * s, (vz - pz) * s, -(vy - py) * s)
pivot_note: Bottom centre of the bench body footprint (1.70 x 0.70 m); vise, saw and offcut overhangs are excluded from the footprint.
front_note: +Y is the working side (vise, drawer, polished edge).
dimensions_note: Occupied extents of the voxel grid (X width, Y depth, Z height).
palette: Shared Claude pilot palette (tools/claude/voxkit.py); one material family per 8-swatch row in MagicaVoxel's palette grid.
collision_hint: Box 1.70 x 0.70 x 0.90 m at the pivot; optional small box for the vise.
story: Home-built garage bench used for years: forearm-polished front edge, a grimy work zone beside the painted vise, a drawer sagging on a broken runner, a mug left behind, a saw hung on the end and the shelf used as storage.
notes: Working surface at 0.90 m; vise top at 1.10 m.
Vise overhangs the front edge by 0.20 m; one offcut pokes 0.10 m past the +X end.
Hand saw hangs on the -X end apron; drawer pulled out 0.10 m with a 5 cm sag.
